title: The Modern-Day Real-Life Golden Goose by Nathan Tabor
outcome: Audit the Golden Goose model alongside a public Bitcoin verification receipt.
show: Make a two-column worksheet for the Golden Goose design and observed Bitcoin records.
concepts: The project models eight processing arms and a waste-to-wealth ledger. Mempool dust, spam flood, orphaned state, and reverse nonce are intake labels in the model.
The design allocates 50% to Core Reserve Vault, 25% to Jet-Siphon Expansion, 15% to Node & Arm Operators, and 10% to Ecosystem & Liquidity.

The proposed refinement stage counts selected packet digests. Its Clean Units, compression ratio, suction velocity multiplier and Golden Eggs are model outputs. Hashing a packet to a smaller digest preserves a fingerprint rather than a recoverable copy of the packet.
The live Golden Goose service checks a public block header against its embedded target. Record any actual pool shares or payouts using their own evidence.
replicate: Apply the allocation percentages to 100 classroom units.
Open the live verifier and write down the block hash and check time. Mark which worksheet cells you can establish from that one receipt.
check: Which of the Golden Egg amounts follows from verifying a public header?
None. The receipt establishes the public header hash and proof check. The percentages belong to the Golden Goose design.
